name: Cadillac Series 452 V-16, 7.4 L OHV (1930-1937)
summary: A 45-degree, long-stroke, low-compression V-16 on an eight-throw crank that fires evenly every 45 degrees. It was built to be nearly silent: at idle the loudest sound was meant to be the ignition points, and at speed the intake roar of two updraft carburettors.

layout.note: Two separate cast-iron eight-cylinder blocks on an aluminium crankcase; pushrod overhead valves.

rod_length_mm.note: Not found. Hagerty says only that the rods were 2.2 in shorter than those of Cadillac's V-8.

compression_ratio.note: Hagerty, drawing on chief engineer Strickland's 1930 technical paper: raised from the V-8's 5.05 to 5.50. Wikipedia's infobox says 5.3:1.

displacement_cc.note: 452 cu in, converted by me. Wikipedia rounds to 7,410 cc.

firing_order.note: Not found on any page opened; cylinder numbering not found either. A search snippet quoted a forum post giving an order attributed to Wikipedia, but the Wikipedia pages I opened (Cadillac V16 engine, Cadillac V-16, V16 engine) do not contain one.

crank.value: Forged steel, eight throws (so the two rods of each opposed pair share a pin), fully counterweighted, 130 lb, five main bearings, harmonic damper.
crank.note: Throw phase angles not printed. Even 45-degree firing with a 45-degree bank and shared pins implies throws arranged like a straight-eight's, 90 degrees apart in firing sequence (my inference).

firing_intervals_deg.note: Hagerty: the 45-degree angle gave 'even 45-degree firing intervals' and 'one power pulse every 45 degrees of crankshaft rotation'.

valves_per_cylinder.note: One intake and one exhaust, single camshaft in the vee, roller followers, pushrods, rocker arms on eccentric pivots with hydraulic lash take-up.

redline_rpm.note: No redline published. Strickland said the valvetrain and ignition still worked 'considerably exceeding 4000 rpm' (Hagerty).

peak_power_kw.note: 165 hp, converted by me. Wikipedia gives 165 hp 'between 3200 and 3400 rpm' for 1930. The 185 hp figure sometimes quoted belongs to the later 1938-1940 135-degree side-valve V-16, a different engine.

peak_torque_nm.note: 320 lb-ft, converted by me; 300 lb-ft or more from 500 to 1,900 rpm.

intake_type.value: carburettors: one Cadillac single-throat updraft carburettor per bank, each feeding a log-type intake manifold bolted to the exhaust manifold for heat

header_type.value: log manifold on the outside of each bank, into dual exhaust pipes (one per bank)
header_type.note: Hagerty: 'Exhaust manifolds bolted to the flanks'; 'Dual exhaust pipes were standard equipment'.

exhaust_notes.value: Tuned for silence: Cadillac's own listening test allowed nothing louder at idle than the click of the ignition points.

sources.what: Hagerty feature 'Sweet V-16: Cadillac's most exotic engine' by Don Sherman, built on William Strickland's 1930 engineering paper; the best technical account I could open.
English Wikipedia Cadillac V16 engine page; infobox figures citing period sources.
